observations: BlockCode contains offsets relative to MainCode, not host pointers.
The three-source and two-destination constructors store opcode into target even though a target argument is passed. This observed behavior is preserved.
EmitAddImmediate tests its unsigned value against both <=127 and >=unsigned(-128); both comparisons are preserved.
The emitter generates x86 instruction bytes algorithmically. No target host-code bytes are embedded or patched.
Runtime signature tables contain 172 named records plus a null sentinel; replacement function pointers are all initially null.
SaveFunctionSignatures writes a .cod file under the application cod directory.
EmitFpuAbsolute at00407EB0 uses IR opcode1000 and emits D9 E1; EmitFpuChangeSign at00407F40 uses IR opcode1003 and emits D9 E0.
EmitAddMemory retains an unused addressSize argument between the original size and address stack arguments.
4202D0 file-pattern scanning belongs to PIF.cpp as FindCICInput;4202C0 sets shared ForcePIFSuccess.

validation.integrated_build: First complete real link passed; no /FORCE

emitter_semantics.scope: Both complete PE images execute their real assembler in Unicorn. Generated bytes and side effects match across integer and FPU opcodes, both widths and buffers, branch widening, label fixups, and guest-address recording. This is behavior validation, not host byte equality.

full_context_probe.scope: Complete unforced /GL /LTCG link with genuine PE relocation records. The other 136 helpers retain their instruction spans and known target constraints; SaveFunctionSignatures remains unmatched, with its 30 target fields not compared because instructions differ. This is not full-image byte equality.

watch_semantics.scope: Original machine-code execution compared with the reconstructed helper emitter traces; count mutation cases verify the do/while entry behavior.

source_recovery_notes: Direct IR array-field assignments restore the original constructor ABIs; local-reference rewrites changed whole-program register allocation.
Binary emitter source/destination formal order is supported by both wrapper instructions and caller argument preparation.
AssembleInstructions uses the shared output cursor while patching labels, restores it afterward, and retries with widened branches. Its complete 4064-byte span matches after relocation normalization.
TrackInstructionChanges switch ordering and fallthroughs reproduce its 816-byte span, including inline tables and alignment.
Valid RecompileSignedBranch callers supply condition values 12..15; both local condition fields are initialized in those four cases. No invented default initialization is present.
RecompileSignedBranch duplicates completion statements in its two source branches; VC7 merges the tails to reproduce the observed register allocation.
CompileBlock selects a ROM-cache byte offset before converting it to a word pointer; both cache read and write paths use the same source structure.

signature_writer_refinement.source_form: The incoming pointer is the advancing instruction cursor. A separate start pointer records the scan base, and the inner for-loop increment resets the hash before the next candidate/signature. Direct signature-table indexing and the original negative filename-separator branch preserve the observed instruction and literal organization.
signature_writer_refinement.callee_abi: Original and candidate receive the input pointer in EAX and copy it to EBX after SUB ESP,0x218; PUSH EBX; PUSH EBP.

remaining_differences: FILE and length use reversed stack slots.
The original reloads and retains the scan base in EBP before the hash-result branch; the candidate uses EBP for FILE during the successful-match calls.
